name: Marram grass
note: Marram grass, Ammophila arenaria (docs/future/13 section 5, P-08, resolution 12). A fibre plant: the walker gathers its leaves in late summer (recipes/world/gather.json marram.leaves), which twist into cord as rushes do, so cord is never stuck on rushes on a sandy island. Drawn with the iris shader (draw: iris; flora-iris.wgsl), so its keys are the iris's: a tussock of fansPerClump fans of stiff, narrow, rolled grey-green blades (leafWidth narrow, little arch, wind.stiffness high), and in summer a few straw spikes (shape.flower spike: spike.widthShare of flowerSize across and lengthShare of it long, a long narrow panicle) above the leaves. Real marram stands 0.6 to 0.9 m, so it is drawn at real size (no drawScale). habitat (docs/future/13 5.3): loose sand above the strandline, 0.8 to 4 m above the sea, dry, tolerating the salt spray, never in the tide band, on dune slopes up to about 35 degrees. growth: the herb defaults of 5.4, drowning under 5 cm of water for 24 hours. It flowers in summer. It is near evergreen: in winter (dormant) it keeps its blades standing at dormantHeight of their height, browner (season.albedo.winter). spread kind rhizome: real marram runs under the sand and binds it into dunes; a mature tussock creeps distanceM away every everyH hours inside spread.window, up to maxCount on the island. volunteer.seasons: summer only. starter: test links only (?plants=fibres, ?plants=all). plantTool false: gather plants are not offered by the Plant tool.
